wording: In a within-subject virtual-reality study (n 50, 39 women), natural scenes elicited more perceived existential danger than artistic ones (22.34 vs 16.38; t(49) -5.72, d -0.81) and somewhat more vastness (29.4 vs 27.18, p 0.047), while self-transcendence, beauty and the overall feeling of the sublime did not differ (sublime BF10 0.164). P101 concludes that there was no significant difference in the capacity of art-based and nature-based stimuli to evoke the sublime.
locator: P101 Introduction to Conclusion, Tables 1-3 (read in full)
counterevidence_limits: Small sample, one VR content set per condition. Slips: the text gives vastness BF01 = 1.033 while Table 2 prints 0.968, and calls vastness and danger 'strong evidence for H 1' although a BF01 near 1 is no evidence either way; the DFAS 'maximum of 15'; ITC-SOPI anchors printed 'strongly disagree' at both ends; an ecological-validity BF printed '100.128.094'.
operationalization: HUM Transcendence = the sublime and self-transcendence elicited by nature and art
verification_phrases: P101|showed no evidence for H 0 (i.e., strong evidence for H 1 ) || P101|perception of vastness (BF 01 = 1.033
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TR0-HUM-01 unchanged (sources read in full in TR0; not re-read in TRA)

wording: P101's Table 2 is internally consistent: Cohen's d = t/sqrt(50) and two-sided p from t(49) reproduce for all eight sublime dimensions (largest gaps 7e-5 and 0.0007), t has the sign of art minus nature throughout, and the printed means, SDs and t imply between-condition correlations of 0.09 to 0.55. One pre-registered check was not supported: Table 2's vastness BF01 is 0.968, so the text's 'strong evidence for H 1' for vastness and danger holds only for danger (BF01 4e-5).
counterevidence_limits: Audits printed numbers; the BF check compares wording with printed values, not a recomputed Bayes factor.
operationalization: HUM Transcendence = auditing a sublime study
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TR0-HUM-02 unchanged (sources read in full in TR0; not re-read in TRA)

wording: Default JZS Bayes factors (Cauchy scale 0.707) recomputed from P101's t and n 50 reproduce all eight printed BF01 within 0.3% (vastness 0.968, danger 3.96e-5), so Table 2 is right and the text's 'BF 01 = 1.033' for vastness is its reciprocal (BF10). Vastness gives no evidence either way (BF01 0.78-1.71 for scales 0.5-1.414), while existential danger gives extreme evidence for a difference at every scale (BF01 below 5e-5).
counterevidence_limits: Assumes JASP's default prior (P101 does not state the scale).
operationalization: HUM Transcendence = recomputing sublime Bayes factors

wording: Applied to P103's paired changes (n 34), default JZS Bayes factors give extreme evidence for change in self-transcendence (BF01 3.5e-8), overall and existential spiritual well-being, depression and negative affect, strong evidence for positive affect (BF01 0.021), and no evidence for religious spiritual well-being (1.30) or life satisfaction (1.45) despite one-tailed p values near .04.
counterevidence_limits: Two-sided default test; P103's design has no control group, so evidence for change is not evidence for an effect of the programme.
operationalization: HUM Transcendence = evidence strength in a self-transcendence intervention
